subject: chemistry-hl
topicLabel: Structure 3.1 — Periodic table & electron structure (Nov unit)

cards.back: Period = row (same number of occupied shells). Group = column (same number of valence electrons → similar chemistry).
Electrons fill sublevels in energy order: 1s 2s 2p 3s 3p 4s 3d 4p … (4s fills before 3d).
An orbital holds at most 2 electrons, with opposite spins.
In degenerate orbitals (same sublevel), electrons occupy singly with parallel spins before pairing.
Energy to remove one mole of electrons from one mole of gaseous atoms to form gaseous ions. Rising trend across a period, falling down a group.
Ability of an atom to attract a shared pair of electrons. Increases across a period, decreases down a group — fluorine is the maximum.
Decreases across a period (same shell, rising nuclear charge). Increases down a group (extra shell + shielding).
Boron's removed electron sits in the higher-energy, more shielded 2p sublevel; beryllium's comes from 2s².
Nitrogen 2p³: three electrons, each alone in a 2p orbital. Oxygen 2p⁴: the 4th electron must pair, and the extra repulsion makes it easier to remove, so IE(O) < IE(N).

cards.front: Successive IE jump — what it reveals
cards.back: A huge jump after the nth ionization = n valence electrons = group number. The (n+1)th electron comes from an inner shell.
Groups 1–2: group number. Groups 13–18: group number − 10. (16 → 6, 17 → 7, 18 → 8.)

cards.front: Which ion is isoelectronic with Ne (10 e⁻)?
cards.back: Na⁺ (11−1). Also O²⁻, Mg²⁺, F⁻. Count protons minus charge — K⁺ and Cl⁻ are argon-like (18).
[Ar]4s² — 4s fills before 3d (aufbau order). [Ar]3d² would be titanium.

cards.front: Why is Na's 2nd ionization energy far larger than its 1st?
cards.back: After losing 3s¹, Na⁺ has the stable 2p⁶ core — the 2nd electron must come from an inner, full shell.
Basic (Na₂O, MgO) → amphoteric (Al₂O₃) → acidic (SiO₂, P₄O₁₀, SO₃). Al₂O₃ reacts with both acids and bases.
Group 1 metals: reactivity INCREASES down (outer electron lost more easily). Group 17 halogens: DECREASES down (electron gain weaker). Opposite directions — common exam trap.

cards.front: Why are group 18 elements so unreactive?
cards.back: Full valence shells (8, or 2 for He) → no drive to gain/lose/share. Monatomic, s/p boundary family.

cards.front: Command term: Explain a trend (vs State it)
cards.back: State = name the trend. Explain = add the mechanism: nuclear charge up, same shell (across) vs more shielding/new shell (down). The reason carries the marks.

cards.front: Full vs condensed configuration — quick method
cards.back: Count electrons = Z. Fill in aufbau order, e.g. Cl (17): 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁵ = [Ne]3s²3p⁵. 4s before 3d until the d block starts.
